hypothesis.cheapest_refuting_observation: `python tools/gdl/slotdiff.py game/g3d/auxanim DoTexModSeqSub` with the second buffer declared: it must print `frame: target 64  ours 72` and exactly the five target-only / five ours-only rows that differ by 8 (`20`/`28`, `24`/`32`, `36`/`44`, `64`/`72`, `-64`/`-72`). If any row breaks the uniform -8 correspondence, the second buffer is not what the target has and the two slots are something else.
hypothesis.count_consequence: count-neutral - the function is T201/O201 at baseline and stayed T201/O201 through all three probes; no probed form changed the instruction count.
hypothesis.screened_against_target: yes - `slotdiff.py game/g3d/auxanim DoTexModSeqSub` was read at baseline (target slots 20 and 24 with 2 uses each, ours slot 28 with 4 uses, every other slot from 32 to 68 identical in both, frame 64 in both) and again with the second buffer declared, where the correspondence became uniform. Not screened: what actually sets the local-block floor in this function.
hypothesis.statement: DoTexModSeqSub needs TWO output buffers, not one: the target passes `&out` at r1+24 in the case -2 arm and at r1+20 in the case -3 arm, two slots with two uses each, while our single `f32 out;` gives one slot at r1+28 with four uses. Declaring the second buffer produces the target's ENTIRE slot map shifted uniformly by +8 - every one of our eleven slots maps onto a target slot at offset-8, gap for gap - so the whole remaining residual is one 8-byte local-block FLOOR difference (ours anchors at r1+28, the target at r1+20), and closing that floor closes the function's slot class outright. The untried construct class is whatever sets that floor: it is not declaration count (adding and removing `kf` moved nothing), not scope (block and function scope returned the same object), and the sibling DoTexModSub in the same TU is byte-exact while making the same 5-argument CalcTexScroll call, so it is not the outgoing-argument width either.
